misconceptions.label: Constant motion requires constant net force
misconceptions.explanation: Believing that an object moving at a constant velocity in space or on ice must have a continuous applied force pushing it forward (Aristotelian misconception).

counterexample.statement: Voyager 1 has traveled billions of kilometers outside our solar system with its engines completely turned off, yet it keeps flying at 61,000 km/h!
counterexample.analogy: Newton's First Law: Objects keep moving at constant velocity unless an external net force (like friction) stops them.

worked_contrast.correct_rule: Constant Velocity implies Net Force = 0; Force causes Acceleration, not velocity.
worked_contrast.explanation: On Earth, things slow down because friction opposes motion, not because motion 'runs out of force'.

probes.prompt: A hockey puck slides across frictionless ice at 10 m/s. What is the net horizontal force acting on it?

options.text: 10 N in the direction of motion

probes.predicted_wrong: 10 N in the direction of motion
probes.rationale: Believing force equals speed confirms the misconception.

practice_questions.prompt: An elevator moves upward at a steady constant speed. How does the cable tension compare to gravity?

questions.prompt: A spacecraft cruises through deep empty space with all thrusters switched off. What happens to its speed?

options.text: It slows down gradually and eventually halts
It continues cruising at the exact same constant speed indefinitely
It accelerates because there is no gravity
It stops immediately when the thruster shuts off
